title: Everest: Gokyo Ri, Chola Pass and Base Camp

source.notes: Rewritten into Brian's chapter format from the YouLi copy. No facts added; open questions are in reviewNotes.

reviewNotes: Price: YouLi has no included/excluded lists for this trip, so both are empty. Is it the same list as the EBC Heli Tour? Is $3,900 per person on double occupancy?
Trail lodging and meals: YouLi gives sleeping altitudes but never says where we sleep on the trek (teahouses?) or which meals are included after day 3. Kathmandu hotel names or areas also not stated.
Gokyo Ri height conflicts: 5,357 m / 17,575 ft in the section text, 5,410 m / 17,750 ft on day 10. I used the day 10 figure. Which is right?
Helicopter: the overview says it shortens the trip by 2–3 days, the section says two full days. I used two. Is the Pheriche–Kathmandu flight inside the $3,900?
Days 1, 2, 11, 13, 16 and 17 use Annapurna trip photos on YouLi. Confirm they suit this page or swap them.

seo.title: Everest: Gokyo Ri, Chola Pass and Base Camp — 17 Days | Adventure Access
seo.description: Seventeen days from Kathmandu: Lukla, Namche, Gokyo Ri, Chola Pass at 17,552 ft, Everest Base Camp and Kala Pathar, then a helicopter back. From $3,900.

hero.title: Gokyo Ri, Chola Pass
hero.subtitle: The long way to Everest Base Camp, over Gokyo Ri and Chola Pass, with a helicopter back to Kathmandu
hero.imageAlt: A line of snow peaks under a dark sky

intro.label: The Journey
intro.heading: More Than Base Camp
paragraphs: This is one of the classic routes in Nepal, and it offers far more than the arrival at Everest Base Camp. From Lukla the trail climbs to Namche Bazaar, then up the Gokyo valley to Gokyo Ri, over Chola Pass, and on to Base Camp and Kala Pathar.

After Base Camp, we arrange a helicopter from Pheriche back to Kathmandu. It saves the long walk down to Lukla, gives a more reliable way out of the region, and on clear days shows you the mountains from the air. Our guides meet you at the airport in Kathmandu and handle the details from there.

dayTypes.label: How the Days Work
dayTypes.heading: Slowly, Slowly
dayTypes.lede: That is the mantra for trekking up the Khumbu. We move at a calculated pace so we do not burn you out early or rush acclimatization. Each trekking day we leave after breakfast, stop for lunch on the trail, and arrive mid-afternoon to rest.

cards.title: City days
cards.body: Days 1–2 and 16–17: arrival, a cultural tour in Boudha, orientation for the trek, and a free day at the end.

cards.title: Trekking days
cards.body: Days 3–14: an average of 4–6 hours on the trail, with longer days of 7–9 hours over Chola Pass, to Base Camp and up Kala Pathar.

cards.title: Acclimatization days
cards.body: Days 5 and 8: climb high, sleep low. A hike to Khumjung from Namche Bazaar, and a rest day in Machherma.

chapters.label: The Journey in Chapters
chapters.heading: Seventeen Days, Three High Points
chapters.lede: Trek times and sleeping altitudes are approximate.

groups.title: Kathmandu — Getting Ready

image.alt: The eyes of Boudhanath stupa under prayer flags

prose: From the moment you meet your guide at the airport, you are in good hands. No need to find your hotel in the back alleys of Boudha or Thamel on your own. There is still plenty of time to explore, eat well, get to know your guide and prepare for the mountains.

days.label: Day 1
days.text: Arrive in Kathmandu, meet your guide and transfer to your hotel.

days.label: Day 2
days.text: A cultural tour in Boudha, the trek orientation, and dinner with your guide and group.

groups.title: Lukla to Namche Bazaar — Into the Khumbu

image.alt: The Lukla runway seen from under a canopy

prose: Lukla is one of the most thrilling airport locations in the world. It sits on a mountainside among Himalayan peaks, and no roads reach it: you fly or you walk. Yak caravans come right to the door to carry supplies toward Namche Bazaar and beyond.

days.label: Day 3
days.text: Fly to Lukla, stop for tea, then a 3–4 hour starter trek down the valley to Phakding at 8,659 ft. Food is provided; pack water and sunscreen.

days.label: Day 4
days.text: About 6–7 hours to Namche Bazaar, including the first steep switchbacks of the valley. Sleep at about 11,316 ft.

days.label: Day 5
days.text: The first acclimatization hike, to Khumjung village and back to Namche. On clear days, your first views of Ama Dablam and Everest.

groups.overnight: 1 Night · Phakding, then 2 Nights · Namche Bazaar

groups.title: Dhole, Machherma and Gokyo — Above the Tree Line

image.alt: A decorated yak on the trail

prose: After Namche Bazaar the serious work begins. The trail leaves the forests behind and climbs well above the tree line, and the land starts to look like the Himalaya you imagined.

days.label: Day 6
days.text: About 7 hours to Dhole. Sleep at about 13,812 ft.

days.label: Day 7
days.text: A shorter 3–4 hours to Machherma. Sleep at about 14,632 ft.

days.label: Day 8
days.text: A day of rest in Machherma to acclimatize.

days.label: Day 9
days.text: About 5 hours to Gokyo Lake. Sleep at about 15,518 ft.

groups.title: Gokyo Ri and Chola Pass — The High Crossing

image.alt: Signposts for Kala Pathar and Everest Base Camp

prose: Gokyo Ri gives panoramic views of the Everest region that you cannot get at Base Camp, where the surrounding peaks block most of the view. From here you see it all from a distance. The next day brings the high crossing of Chola Pass.

days.label: Day 10
days.text: A 2.5 km hike to the summit of Gokyo Ri, then 3–4 hours of trekking to Dragnag. Sleep at about 15,420 ft.

days.label: Day 11
days.text: About 7–8 hours over Chola Pass, high point 17,552 ft, to Dzonglha. Sleep at about 15,879 ft.

groups.title: Everest Base Camp and Kala Pathar

image.alt: Trekkers crossing a wide valley below steep mountains

prose: Two days in the Base Camp region to make the most of it. The visit puts you on the Khumbu Glacier with time to explore part of the site, then Kala Pathar, the highest point of the trip, before the walk down to Pheriche.

days.label: Day 12
days.text: About 4–5 hours to Lobuche. Sleep at about 16,109 ft.

days.label: Day 13
days.text: About 7–8 hours from Lobuche to Everest Base Camp and on to Gorak Shep. Sleep at about 16,995 ft.

days.label: Day 14
days.text: Climb Kala Pathar, 18,448 ft at the summit, then down to Pheriche. About 8–9 hours. Sleep at about 13,812 ft.

groups.title: Pheriche to Kathmandu — By Helicopter

image.alt: A red helicopter flying past snowy mountains

prose: The helicopter shortens the trek by two full days and gives a more reliable departure from the region. On clear days, the mountains go by your window all the way back to Kathmandu.

days.label: Day 15
days.text: Fly by helicopter from Pheriche to Kathmandu, with aerial views of the Himalaya.

days.label: Day 16
days.text: A free day in Kathmandu: rest, revisit favorite places from the start of the trip, and repack.

days.label: Day 17
days.text: Your guide picks you up at the hotel and takes you to the airport for your flight.

pullQuote: Slowly, slowly. This is the mantra for trekking up the Khumbu Valley.

goodToKnow.label: Good to Know
goodToKnow.heading: Before You Go
goodToKnow.lede: A few things that shape how this trip runs.

cards.title: Kathmandu
cards.body: Your guide meets you at the airport and takes care of the details, so you can take in the city. Your time there includes good food, getting to know your guide, and an orientation for the trek.

cards.title: Pace
cards.body: Itineraries are built around an average of 4–6 hours of trekking a day. Expect several steep switchbacks, starting on the climb to Namche Bazaar.

cards.title: Altitude
cards.body: Climb high, sleep low. On acclimatization days we hike higher, often to viewpoints, then return to sleep at the same altitude. This helps your body adjust and reduces the risk of altitude sickness.

cards.title: Views of Everest
cards.body: Base Camp is so close to Everest that it gives little view of the mountain. Gokyo Ri shows it from a distance, in a way few trekking points in the region can.

cards.title: The flight out
cards.body: A helicopter from Pheriche to Kathmandu saves two days of walking down to Lukla and gives a more reliable departure from the region.
